title: setNudgePaymentToken does not validate that the new token is non-trivial, allowing nudge of arbitrary contract
description: No EOA / contract / interface check is performed on `newToken`. Setting `nudgePaymentToken` to an EOA, a self-destructed contract, or a contract that does not implement ERC20 will cause the runtime `IERC20(_nudgeTokenEntry).balanceOf(address(this))` call inside `batchMint` to revert (or, for a non-implementor, return arbitrary garbage), DoSing the nudge code path and potentially DoSing all qualifying batchMints. Because the failure mode is runtime, the misconfiguration is not caught at setter time.
exploit_scenario: 1) Owner accidentally pastes the wrong address into `setNudgePaymentToken` (e.g. an EOA from their address book). 2) Subsequent `batchMint` calls with `count >= nudgeSize` revert at line 144 because `balanceOf` reverts on the EOA. 3) All large batches DoS until owner re-runs the setter with the correct token.
recommended_mitigation: Validate at setter time: `(bool ok, bytes memory data) = newToken.staticcall(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20.balanceOf.selector, address(this))); require(ok && data.length >= 32, "BatchMint: invalid nudge token");`. Or require `newToken.code.length > 0` for a basic contract check.
notes: Operational hazard. Project's known-issues policy may treat misconfiguration as 'reckless admin mistake' (out of scope). Filed as QA.
